gloss: promptly, right after; as soon as

definitions.explanation: Doing something quickly or immediately, without wasting time.
Used as a suffix after nouns indicating a time or event to mean 'right after' or 'as soon as.' Read as そうそう in this usage.

examples.japanese: {早々|そうそう}に{切|き}り{上|あ}げた。
{会議|かいぎ}が{終|お}わると、{早々|そうそう}に{帰|かえ}ってしまった。
examples.english: As soon as the meeting ended, he went straight home.

examples.japanese: {忙|いそが}しかったので、{挨拶|あいさつ}{早々|そうそう}に{失礼|しつれい}した。
examples.english: I was busy, so I excused myself right after the greetings.

examples.japanese: {入社|にゅうしゃ}{早々|そうそう}、{大|おお}きなプロジェクトを{任|まか}された。
examples.english: Right after joining the company, I was entrusted with a big project.

examples.japanese: {新年|しんねん}{早々|そうそう}、うれしいニュースが{届|とど}いた。
examples.english: Right at the start of the new year, good news arrived.

examples.japanese: {開店|かいてん}{早々|そうそう}にお{客|きゃく}さんが{行列|ぎょうれつ}を{作|つく}っていた。
examples.english: Right after opening, customers were already lining up.

notes:
USAGE:
Two main patterns:
1. {早々|そうそう}に + verb: promptly, without delay (adverbial)
2. Noun + {早々|そうそう}: right after [noun], as soon as [noun] (suffix)

The suffix pattern attaches to nouns representing events or time points: {入社|にゅうしゃ}{早々|そうそう} (right after joining), {新年|しんねん}{早々|そうそう} (right at the new year), {到着|とうちゃく}{早々|そうそう} (right after arriving).

Note: This is different from the colloquial filler word そうそう (meaning 'oh right, that reminds me').

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {早々|そうそう}に{引|ひ}き{上|あ}げる: to withdraw promptly
- {新年|しんねん}{早々|そうそう}: right at the start of the new year
- {入社|にゅうしゃ}{早々|そうそう}: right after joining a company
